{"title":"The Dino Team by the Sea","level":2,"topic":"dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads a page about dinosaurs. The page says dinosaurs were real!

She dreams of a team of dinosaurs by the sea.

One is big. His name is Oak. Oak has a long neck. He eats leaves all day. He eats and eats.

One is small. Her name is Rain. Rain likes to run on the trail. She can leap! She can wait, then leap again!

A big boat floats near the sea. Oak sees it. Rain sees it too.

"Can we sail?" says Rain.

"We are too big!" says Oak. "The boat may not float!"

So they stay on the sand. They play in the rain. They eat green leaves and soak their feet.

The sun goes down. The sea is quiet. Oak and Rain sleep by the oak tree.

Maya wakes up. She reads one more page. Dinosaurs are the best!","cover_scene":"A long-necked green dinosaur and a small speedy dinosaur standing together on a sandy beach at sunset, with a little boat floating on the waves behind them."}

{"title":"Coach Toad and the Dino Race","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur race","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Coach Toad blows his whistle. "Time to race!"

Three dinosaurs wait by the oak. Their feet make the road shake.

"On your mark!" says Coach Toad. "Ready? Go!"

The first dino is Beak. Beak can leap way up high. She can reach a leaf on a tall tree.

The next dino is Coal. Coal is big. Coal runs slow, but he keeps on going.

The last dino is Gail. Gail loves the rain. She splashes down the trail. Mud sprays on her tail!

Beak leaps. Coal groans. Gail sails past!

Then Beak sees Coal. Coal is stuck in deep mud. Beak stops. Gail stops too.

They each pull. They heave! Pop! Coal is free.

All three cross the line at the same time.

"A tie!" says Coach Toad. "You are a team!"

They eat green leaves by the sea and cheer.","cover_scene":"Three cheerful dinosaurs lined up at a muddy racing trail while a small toad in a cap holds up a whistle, big oak tree behind them."}

{"title":"Dean Digs Up a Dino Egg","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur fossils","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Dean is on a dig team. He digs in the heat all day.

His pail is full of dirt. His feet ache. But Dean will not quit.

Tap, tap. His pick hits something hard.

"Wait!" says Dean. "I see a shape!"

He sweeps the dirt away. It is an egg! A real dino egg, made of stone.

Dean's mom leans in close. "This egg is old," she says. "Way old."

They load the egg on a train. The train goes down the coast to a big hall.

Now the egg sits on a stand. Kids come to peek at it.

One kid asks, "Did a dino leap out?"

Dean grins. "Long ago, maybe! Some dinos ate meat. Some ate leaves. They ran fast on the plain."

Dean paints a sign for the egg. He reads it out loud: THE DINO EGG. FOUND BY DEAN.","cover_scene":"A boy in a sun hat kneeling in a dusty desert dig site, brushing dirt off a large speckled stone dinosaur egg."}

Five: a leaf, turned to stone.

{"title":"Maya Draws a Dinosaur","level":2,"topic":"drawing dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya sat with a pad and a pen. "Today I will draw a dinosaur," she said.

On the screen, a museum page showed her how.

First, draw the tail. Make it long and thin.

Next, draw the back. It goes up like a hill by the road.

Now the neck. This dino ate leaves, so the neck must reach high.

Draw a small head. Add one bright eye. Add a beak.

Four legs. Big feet. Each foot needs three toes.

Maya leaned in close. She was almost done.

Last, she painted it green with gray spots. She painted a gold sun and a stream.

"Wait!" said Maya. "It needs a name."

She wrote: SEA-TAIL, THE LEAF EATER.

Mom came in. "Oh! That dino looks real!"

Maya beamed. She taped it on the wall and made a new page.","cover_scene":"A girl at a desk drawing a big green long-necked dinosaur on paper, crayons scattered around her."}

{"title":"Spiney Goes Fishing","level":2,"topic":"spinosaurus fishing","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Long ago, a big dino lived near a wide stream in Africa. Kids call him Spiney.

Spiney was the biggest meat eater of all. He was taller than a jeep!

He stood in the cool water. His feet sank in the gray mud. He kept still. He did not speak.

Then a fish swam near. Snap! Spiney got his meal.

His long tail helped him swim. It beat back and forth like a paddle. Few dinos could do that!

When the sun beat down, Spiney lay on the beach. His tall sail soaked up the heat.

At sea, big beasts swam deep. But Spiney stayed close to the coast.

Maya read each fact. "Spiney," she said, "you are my team pick!"","cover_scene":"A huge sail-backed dinosaur standing chest-deep in a wide river, snapping at a silvery fish, palm trees on the bank."}

She brushed fast. Sand flew. A long, smooth, white thing stuck out of the ground.

A pod glided through the cold gray water, black and white and gleaming. The smallest calf stayed close to his mother.

Orcas are clever. They make plans. When a school of fish drifted past, the pod did not simply crash into it. They swam in a slow circle and pressed the fish into a tight, spinning ball. Then, one by one, each orca took a turn to feed.

Orcas are not fish. Like whales, they must climb to the top for a breath of fresh air. Whoosh! Spray flew from the blowholes.

Then the pod began to speak, with clicks and squeaks and long whistles that traveled for miles.

Maya grinned. "A whole family, talking under the sea."","cover_scene":"A pod of black and white orcas swimming together in cold blue water, a small calf close beside its mother."}

Jean does not mind. She swims to meet her pod.

Orcas eat fish. They eat squid. They eat big things and small things.

Jean leaps high. Her tail slaps the sea. Splash! The spray soaks the ice.

She was floating in a boat on the cold Arctic sea. Beside her, an orca rose up, breathing out a plume of mist. Then, from the deep green water, a huge head appeared — a sail-backed dinosaur!

{"title":"Night at the Dinosaur Hall","level":3,"topic":"dinosaur museum","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya won a contest: one whole night sleeping in the dinosaur hall!

She spread her sleeping bag beneath the great long-necked skeleton. The lights went low. The room grew quiet.

Then she heard a creak.

The huge beast lowered its head and peered down at her. "Do you mean to sleep right there?" it said.

Maya squeaked. "You can speak?"

"Only at night," the dinosaur said. "Come. I will teach you what the signs leave out."

They roamed the hall. The dinosaur explained how it reached the highest leaves, how its team moved in a herd, and how it drank from a stream each dawn.

"Scientists keep learning new things about us," it said proudly. "Each year they find more."

At daybreak the bones went still again.

Maya rolled up her sleeping bag, beaming. She had the best dream — or maybe it was real.","cover_scene":"A girl in a sleeping bag looking up at a towering long-necked dinosaur skeleton in a dim museum hall at night."}

"How loud is that?" Dad asked.

"Loud enough to shake the ground," she said. "Loud enough to wake a dinosaur."

So Maya built one. She taped three paper towel tubes together, painted them gleaming white, and drew a green dinosaur on the side.

That night she dreamed her rocket reached the moon. A long-necked dinosaur waited there, munching moon leaves, and waved a tiny claw as she flew past.

"See you again soon!" Maya called, and her voice boomed louder than thunder.","cover_scene":"A girl in a driveway launching a homemade paper rocket painted with a green dinosaur, autumn leaves swirling around her."}

chapters.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
chapters.text:
Maya reads about dinosaurs each day.

Today she reads a tale of a dino team by the sea.

Big Rex eats meat. He has a loud roar. His feet make deep tracks in the sand.

Small Nia eats leaves. She is neat and quick. She can see far down the coast road.

Rain falls. The team needs a dry place to wait.

"This way!" Nia calls. She leads them up the trail.

They reach a cave. It is safe and dry. The team sleeps in a heap.

At dawn, the sun beams on the sea. The rain has gone.

Rex and Nia eat a snack and play on the beach.

Then they load big rocks on a boat and float away.

Maya shuts the book. Real scientists dig up dino bones each year. They team up to teach us more!

Maya wants to dig too. Some day, she will.

chapters.title: Rain on the Dino Trail
chapters.text:
Deep in the green oak woods, a big dino sleeps.

Her name is Oat. She eats leaves all day.

Today, rain falls on the trail. Drip, drip, drip!

Oat lifts her head. She sees a snail on a leaf.

"Wait!" says Oat. "Do not soak, little snail."

Oat picks up the leaf with her beak. She keeps the snail dry.

The rain makes a road of mud. Oat's feet sail and slide!

Soon the sun peeks out. The trail is clean and bright.

Oat sets the snail in the grass. The snail eats a green leaf. What a treat!

Oat goes back to her nest to sleep.

Did you know real people still find dino bones today? Scientists dig them up and teach us new facts each year. We may learn about a dino just like Oat!

Dream on, Oat. Dream on, snail.

transcript.title: Dean Digs Up a Dino Egg
transcript.text:
Dean is on a dig team. He digs in the heat all day.

His pail is full of dirt. His feet ache. But Dean will not quit.

Tap, tap. His pick hits something hard.

"Wait!" says Dean. "I see a shape!"

He sweeps the dirt away. It is an egg! A real dino egg, made of stone.

Dean's mom leans in close. "This egg is old," she says. "Way old."

They load the egg on a train. The train goes down the coast to a big hall.

Now the egg sits on a stand. Kids come to peek at it.

One kid asks, "Did a dino leap out?"

Dean grins. "Long ago, maybe! Some dinos ate meat. Some ate leaves. They ran fast on the plain."

Dean paints a sign for the egg. He reads it out loud: THE DINO EGG. FOUND BY DEAN.

chapters.title: The Dino Boat Goes Green
chapters.text:
Tay the dino had a green boat. The boat could float!

Tay ate a big meal of leaves. Then he set sail.

"Sail with me!" Tay said to Jean.

Jean the dino ran down the trail. She had a pail of seeds and a coat.

The boat did not leak. It did float on the deep sea.

Rain fell. Drip, drip! Jean put on her coat.

Tay saw a seal! The seal ate a fish and gave a squeal.

"Wait!" said Jean. "I see land!"

They sailed to the beach. The sand was clean and pale.

Jean planted her seeds by the oak tree. Soon green leaves would grow.

Tay read a book about real dinosaurs. It said dinosaurs lived long ago, and each day people learn new things about them!

"We are real," said Tay.

Jean gave a big cheer. "Yes! And we sail!"

transcript.title: The Dino Bone Hunt at the Museum
transcript.text:
Maya got a note. It said: COME TO THE DINO HUNT!

She rode the train to the museum. Rain fell on the road.

A guide with a green coat said, "Each kid gets a list. Find eight dino things!"

Maya read her list.

One: a big claw. She found it. It was as long as her arm!

Two: a tail bone. It lay in a case.

Three: a beak. Some dinos had beaks like birds.

Four: a tooth. This tooth ate meat!

Five: a leaf, turned to stone.

Six: a dino egg.

Seven: a foot print in gray clay.

Eight: the tall neck of a beast by the stairs.

Maya got them all. The guide gave her a gold seal.

"You are a real dino team player," he said.

Maya beamed all the way home.

chapters.title: Dino Seeds on the Green Hill
chapters.text:
Dean is a big dino. He eats leaves all day.

Today Dean has a pail of seeds. He will plant them on the green hill.

Rain drips on his tail. Dean does not mind the rain. Rain helps seeds grow.

A snail slides by. "Wait!" says Dean. "Do not eat my seeds!"

The snail eats one leaf and goes back to the road.

Soon the sun is out. Dean sits by an oak tree and takes a nap.

When he wakes, he sees green! Tiny green leaves peek up from the soil.

Dean gives a happy roar. He will have a feast each day!

Real kids can read about dinos like Dean on Nat Geo Kids. There are facts, games, and art. Real teams dig up dino bones and teach us how they ate.

Dean would say, "Eat your greens!"

transcript.title: Maya Draws a Dinosaur
transcript.text:
Maya sat with a pad and a pen. "Today I will draw a dinosaur," she said.

On the screen, a museum page showed her how.

First, draw the tail. Make it long and thin.

Next, draw the back. It goes up like a hill by the road.

Now the neck. This dino ate leaves, so the neck must reach high.

Draw a small head. Add one bright eye. Add a beak.

Four legs. Big feet. Each foot needs three toes.

Maya leaned in close. She was almost done.

Last, she painted it green with gray spots. She painted a gold sun and a stream.

"Wait!" said Maya. "It needs a name."

She wrote: SEA-TAIL, THE LEAF EATER.

Mom came in. "Oh! That dino looks real!"

Maya beamed. She taped it on the wall and made a new page.

chapters.title: The Dino Team Reads the Facts
chapters.text:
Meet the dino team! They like to read.

Rae reads a neat book about dinosaurs. The book has facts and big art. Real scientists dig and find new dino bones each year!

"Read it to me!" says Joan.

Rae reads: "Some dinos ate leaves. Some ate meat. Some had a long tail and a beak."

Joan leaps up. "I eat leaves too!" she says. She munches a green leaf by the road.

Rae reads more. "One dino could reach a treetop. One could sail on big feet down a dirt trail."

The team sits by the sea and reads all day. The sun is a warm beam on each back.

"Dinos are the best," says Joan. "Can we read it again?"

Rae grins. "Yes! Let's read it again and again."

So the dino team reads, and reads, and reads.

transcript.title: Spike the Sail-Back Dino
transcript.text:
Maya sat down to draw again. Today the lesson was a sail-back dino!

"Draw a long snout," said the man on the screen. "Like a boat!"

Maya drew it. Then she drew the sail on his back. It was tall and wide.

She named him Spike.

Spike lived by a deep stream long ago. He did not eat leaves. He ate fish!

Splash! Spike dips his snout in. He waits. He waits. Then he snaps!

A fish! Spike eats it in one gulp.

The day gets hot. Spike's sail soaks up the heat. Then he cools in the stream.

Rain falls. Spike walks on the muddy coast. His feet leave deep prints.

Maya read that Spike was real. He was bigger than a school bus!

She taped Spike next to her last dino. "Now they are a team," she said.

chapters.title: Dino Beak and the Big Feast
chapters.text:
Bea is a dino with a big beak.

Today Bea will have a feast by the stream.

She eats leaves. She eats green peas. She eats a peach from a tree.

"Eat with me!" Bea squeaks.

Her team comes. Each dino eats a treat.

One dino eats seaweed. One dino eats beans. One dino eats wheat.

Then Bea sees a neat book near the stream.

She reads it. She reads slow. She reads it again.

The book tells real dino facts. Kids read facts like this at Nat Geo Kids! It has games and art and new science, too.

Bea reads that some dinos had a beak like hers. Some ate meat. Some ate leaves, like Bea.

"I eat leaves!" Bea peeps. "I am real!"

Her team cheers by the stream.

Bea reads the book each week.

Each time she reads, she can read it faster.

What a neat feast. What a neat team.

transcript.title: Spiney Goes Fishing
transcript.text:
Long ago, a big dino lived near a wide stream in Africa. Kids call him Spiney.

Spiney was the biggest meat eater of all. He was taller than a jeep!

Each day Spiney went to the stream to eat. He did not eat leaves. He ate fish.

He stood in the cool water. His feet sank in the gray mud. He kept still. He did not speak.

Then a fish swam near. Snap! Spiney got his meal.

His long tail helped him swim. It beat back and forth like a paddle. Few dinos could do that!

When the sun beat down, Spiney lay on the beach. His tall sail soaked up the heat.

At sea, big beasts swam deep. But Spiney stayed close to the coast.

Maya read each fact. "Spiney," she said, "you are my team pick!"

chapters.title: Dino Beach Team Clean-Up
chapters.text:
The dino team went to the beach. The sun was hot. The sea was blue.

"Let's clean the beach!" said Pete. Pete is a big green dino.

The team read a sign by the sea. The sign said: Keep the beach neat!

Pete reads it again. "We can do that," he said.

The team ate a snack first. They ate peas and a peach. Then they got to work.

Pete hauled a heap of cans. Jean picked up beads and a teal cup. Dean got an old sail from the boat.

Soon the beach was clean! The team sat and ate one last treat.

"Real dinos ate leaves and meat," said Jean. "But they did not eat cans!"

The team read that fact in a book. Kids can read dino facts too, and see dino art.

Pete let out a big squeak. "I love my team!"

transcript.title: The Big Dig in the Sand
transcript.text:
Big news! A team of diggers found a whole Spinosaurus skeleton in the sand.

Maya read the story twice. Then she grabbed her spade.

"I will dig too," she said.

She went to the sand by the steps. Scrape, scrape, scrape. The sand slid off her spade.

Flat stones. A stick. A small crab shell. Maya kept digging.

Her brush swept the dust away. Something black! She brushed again. It was a spoon.

Maya grinned. "Not a dino. But it is still a find!"

She stood and stretched. Then her spade clinked on something hard.

She brushed fast. Sand flew. A long, smooth, white thing stuck out of the ground.

A bone! A real bone!

Dad knelt down to check it. "That is from a big fish," he said. "Still, a great dig!"

Maya put it in her glass jar and smiled.

chapters.title: Dino Dave Makes a Cave
chapters.text:
Dino Dave had a home in a cave.

The cave was safe. The cave was wide.

Dave made a nice den inside.

He had one bone, one stone, one pine cone.

"I like my cave," said Dave. "It is mine alone."

Then came rain. Big drops! Splat, splat!

A small dino sat by a lake. She was Jane.

Jane was wet. Jane shook. Jane shivered.

"Come in!" said Dave. "My cave can take five!"

Jane came inside. She was safe and dry.

Dave gave Jane the bone. Jane gave Dave a smile.

They made a fine game with the stone.

Roll it. Chase it. Hide it. Find it!

When the rain was done, the sun came out.

"I like this cave," said Jane. "And I like you."

"Same!" said Dave.

Scientists still dig up dino bones today. They find new facts all the time. Maybe one day they will find Dave's cave!

transcript.title: Stomp, Stomp, Skeleton!
transcript.text:
Maya clicked on a fun dino game. The screen said: BUILD A SKELETON!

A pile of bones spun on the screen. Maya had to drag each one to the right spot.

First, the skull. Click! It snapped into place.

Next, the spine. Twelve small blocks in a straight line. Click, click, click.

Then the ribs. They bend like a basket.

Maya stopped. Where did the flat bone go? She slid it up. Wrong. She slid it down. Snap! Right!

Now the legs. Strong and thick. And last, the long tail that drags on the ground.

The screen flashed. STAND BACK!

The skeleton stood up. It stomped. It swung its tail. It let out a big roar!

Maya clapped and clapped.

"Play again?" asked the screen.

"Yes!" said Maya. "Ten more times!"

chapters.title: Chomp the Dino Checks the Shells
chapters.text:
Chomp is a dino with thick, thumping feet.

Chomp went to the shore to check the shells. Shell after shell! Chomp did not munch them. He just wished to see them.

"Which shell is the best?" Chomp said.

A thin shell. A chunky shell. A shell with a chip in it.

Then Chomp saw something. Not a shell! It was a tooth. A big, sharp dino tooth in the sand.

"Whose tooth is this?" Chomp said with a gasp.

A shark swished by. "Not mine!" said the shark.

Chomp thought and thought. The tooth was old. Older than Chomp. Older than the shore.

Chomp put the tooth on a flat dish and took it home.

Scientists find dino teeth and bones like this. They dig, they brush, and they learn. Each tooth tells a tale of dinos long ago.

Chomp was such a good digger. What a find!

transcript.title: Which Dino Is Which?
transcript.text:
Maya found a match game on the museum page. Eight fossil photos. Eight names. Which one is which?

Photo one: a thick skull with three sharp horns. "That is a Triceratops!" said Maya. Check!

Photo two: a long neck that reached high. It munched on shrubs and branches. Check!

Photo three: a chomping jaw with teeth as long as her hand. "T. rex!" she whispered. Check!

Photo four: a shell on its back, thick as a dish. Check!

Photo five: a whip tail with a club on the end. Whack! Check!

Photo six: a dino with a crest like a trumpet. It could chirp a song. Check!

Photo seven: a small one with sharp claws. Check!

Photo eight: a wide sail. "Spiney!" Maya cheered. Check!

Eight matches! The screen flashed stars. Maya wished for more.

chapters.title: Shep the Dino and the Thick Fish Path
chapters.text:
Shep is a dino with a short tail. Shep likes fish.

She chats with Chip. "Let's go fish!" says Shep.

They dash down a thin path. The path is thick with mush.

Splash! Shep steps in a ditch. Chip helps Shep up.

Then they reach the shore. Fish flash in the shallow water.

Shep will catch a fish. Chomp! She has a big fish.

Chip will catch a fish too. Chomp! He has a fat fish.

They munch and munch. "This fish is rich!" says Chip.

Then Shep sees a shell. It has a thin crack.

"Shall we check it?" asks Chip.

They check the shell. A tiny dino hatches! Chirp, chirp!

Shep and Chip cheer.

Science folks say dinos did hatch from shells, just like chicks!

Shep will teach the little one to fish.

What a fresh, fun day on the path!

transcript.title: The Dino Shell and the Octopus
transcript.text:
Maya went to the aquarium. She saw a real octopus!

It had eight arms. Each arm had a long stripe. The octopus slid on the glass and turned pink, then white.

"Shhh," said Maya. "He is shy."

Next to the tank was a shelf with a big shell. A sign said: THIS SHELL IS 90 MILLION YEARS OLD.

Maya put her chin on her hands. Long ago, sea beasts swam where fish swim now. Some had sharp teeth. Some had thick shells.

A man in a blue shirt came by. "Which one do you like?" he asked.

"That shell," said Maya. "And the octopus."

"Then you like both," he said. "Old and new."

Maya nodded. She wished she could watch all day.

She drew the octopus when she got home. Eight arms. Not one less!

chapters.title: Shelly the Sea Turtle
chapters.text:
Shelly is a sea turtle. She has a thick shell on her back.

Shelly swims in the ship's shade. She dips and she splashes.

A fish swims up. "Which way to the shore?" the fish asks.

"This way!" says Shelly. "Push with me!"

They rush past shells. They rush past a chunk of rock.

Chip the crab has a chat with them. "Check that shape!" says Chip.

It is a chest! Shelly gives it a shove. Chomp! The lid shuts.

Then the lid shifts. Inside are shiny shells, thin and thick.

"Thanks, Shelly!" says the fish.

Here is a fun fact: sea turtles can hold their breath for a long, long time. They go deep, then push up for air.

Shelly shuts her eyes in the sun. Chip chats. The fish splashes.

What a rich day on this shore!

transcript.title: Five Giants of the Deep
transcript.text:
Long ago, the ocean was full of giants. Maya watched a show about five of them.

The first had a long neck and a fat body. It swam with four flat fins. Whoosh! It was called a plesiosaur.

The next one was a fish-shaped beast with big eyes. It could dash and catch fish in the dark.

The third was thick and strong. Its jaw could crunch a shell to bits. Chomp!

The fourth had sharp teeth and a whip-like tail. It was as long as a bus.

The fifth was the champ. The biggest! It shook the water when it swam.

"Which one is best?" asked Dad.

Maya thought and thought. "All of them," she said.

Then she splashed in the bath and swished her hand like a fin.

chapters.title: The Fish with a Wish
chapters.text:
Chicago has a big fish home. It is the Shedd Aquarium.

In a tank, a tiny egg sat. Shh! Do not shake it.

Then the egg went pop! Out came a baby frogfish. It had thin fins and a fat chin.

"What a champ!" said Chad. "No one has ever raised this fish from an egg."

Chad and Beth check the tank each day. They check the chill of the water. They check the shell bits on the sand.

The frogfish does not dash. It does not swish. It walks on its fins like a chubby cat!

It munches shrimp. Chomp, chomp, chomp!

Beth had a wish. "I wish this fish will help us raise much more fish."

Then the frogfish hid by a shell and went shh.

What a fish. What a champ. What a day at the Shedd!

transcript.title: Three Hearts and a Big Blue Whale
transcript.text:
"Did you know?" said Maya. "An octopus has three hearts!"

Dad laughed. "Then what has the biggest heart?"

Maya thought. "A whale?"

"Yes! The blue whale. Its heart is as big as a chair."

They watched a show on the couch. A blue whale swam by, long as three school buses. It was the biggest thing that ever lived. Bigger than a Spinosaurus!

A whale is not a fish. A whale must come up to breathe. Whoosh! Air shoots up in a tall spray.

Next came a whale shark. It has spots like white chalk. It munches tiny shrimp.

Then a manta ray flew past, flapping like a huge kite.

"Sharks, whales, rays," said Maya. "And an octopus with three hearts."

She shut her eyes and wished she could swim with them all.

chapters.title: Chip the Octopus and the Shell Shop
chapters.text:
Chip is an octopus. Chip has a shop. It is a shell shop on the ocean floor.

"Shells for sale! Shells for sale!" Chip shouts. "Chat with me and check my shells!"

A fish swims up. The fish wants a thin shell. Chip picks the thin one. "Thanks!" says the fish.

A crab comes next. The crab wants a fat shell with a chip in it. Chip finds it. "Thanks!" says the crab.

Then a dolphin rushes in. She has much to tell.

"I have a baby!" she says. "My baby was born tail first! That is how dolphins come. Tail, then chin, then nose!"

Chip shakes all eight arms. What a shock! What a thrill!

"Shall I pick a shell for the baby?" Chip asks.

He picks a shiny shell shaped like a dish.

The dolphin says, "Thank you, Chip!"

Chip shouts, "Shells for sale!" and the shop is full again.

transcript.title: The Orca Pod Plan
transcript.text:
Maya read that orcas swim in family groups called pods. Every orca in a pod knows the others, just like a class knows every kid.

A pod glided through the cold gray water, black and white and gleaming. The smallest calf stayed close to his mother.

Orcas are clever. They make plans. When a school of fish drifted past, the pod did not simply crash into it. They swam in a slow circle and pressed the fish into a tight, spinning ball. Then, one by one, each orca took a turn to feed.

Orcas are not fish. Like whales, they must climb to the top for a breath of fresh air. Whoosh! Spray flew from the blowholes.

Then the pod began to speak, with clicks and squeaks and long whistles that traveled for miles.

Maya grinned. "A whole family, talking under the sea."

chapters.title: The Crab and the Flip Club
chapters.text:
Crab had a club. It was the Flip Club.

"Flip! Flap! Flop!" said Crab. "Come and swim with me!"

A crib of baby dolphins swam up fast. Did you know? A baby dolphin is born tail-first! Tail first, then the rest.

"Can we flip?" they said.

"Yes!" said Crab. "Flip Club is free!"

Crab sat on a flat rock. Crabs cannot flip. Crabs just crawl and creep.

The dolphins did a flip. They did a big flop. Foam and spray flew up!

"Crack!" A crab claw clapped. "Fine flip!" said Crab.

Then a flat fish swam by. "Can I flip?" said the fish.

"Flip Club is for all!" said Crab.

Fish flipped. Dolphins flipped. Crab did a slow crawl on the crest of a wave.

"Flip! Flap! Flop!" they all sang. "Flip Club! Flip Club!"

And the crab on the rock was the best fan of all.

transcript.title: The Orca and the Ice
transcript.text:
An orca swims in the cold sea. Her name is Jean.

Jean is big. She weighs as much as six cars! Her back is black. Her side is white like snow.

Today she sees a seal. The seal sleeps on a sheet of ice.

Jean dives deep. Then she speeds up fast. Whack! She bumps the ice.

The ice shakes. The seal wakes up and leaps away. This time the seal is safe!

Jean does not mind. She swims to meet her pod.

Orcas eat fish. They eat squid. They eat big things and small things.

Jean leaps high. Her tail slaps the sea. Splash! The spray soaks the ice.

Her pod calls out. Squeak! Click! Jean calls back.

Then they swim away, deep in the green sea, to play all day.
transcript.cover_scene: A black and white orca leaping out of icy blue water near a floating ice sheet, spray flying.

chapters.title: Flip the Baby Dolphin
chapters.text:
A baby dolphin is born tail-first! That is true.

Mom calls him Flip.

Flip must swim up fast for his first breath. Flap, flap! Up he goes. He blows a puff of mist.

Flip likes to flip. He likes to flop. He likes to flap his tail on the flat blue sea.

A crab named Cram sits on a crack in a rock.

"Can you flip?" asks Flip.

"No," says Cram. "But I can crawl. Crawl, crawl, crawl!"

Flip and Cram play by the cliff. Crash! A wave hits the rock. Cram grabs a clam shell and holds on.

Flip flips up. Flip flops down. Splash!

Cram claps his claws. "You are the best flipper in the sea!"

Flip swims back to Mom. He is glad.

Flap, flip, flop, crawl, crash, clap. What a fun day in the blue sea!

transcript.title: The Dinosaur That Swam With Orcas
transcript.text:
Maya had a strange, wonderful dream.

She was floating in a boat on the cold Arctic sea. Beside her, an orca rose up, breathing out a plume of mist. Then, from the deep green water, a huge head appeared — a sail-backed dinosaur!

"You are meant to be extinct," Maya said.

"I dreamed my way here," the dinosaur replied. "I came to meet the biggest beasts of today."

The orca squeaked a greeting. She showed him how her pod hunts as a team, sweeping fish into a tight, spinning heap.

The dinosaur showed her how he waited in a shallow stream, still as stone, then snapped up a gleaming fish in his long jaws.

"We both eat fish," he said. "We are not so different after all."

Maya woke, reached for her paints, and painted them side by side beneath a pale sun.
transcript.cover_scene: A sail-backed dinosaur and a black and white orca meeting nose to nose in icy ocean water beside a small wooden boat.

chapters.title: Glad the Dolphin and the Blue Clam
chapters.text:
Glad is a dolphin. She swims in the blue sea.

Glad sees a clam on a flat rock. The clam is blue too!

"Click, click!" says Glad. "Come play!"

The clam claps shut. Clap! Clap!

A crab creeps close. The crab has big claws.

"Do not crack my clam," says Glad.

The crab grins. "I will not. I just want to play."

Glad does a flip. The crab does a flop. The clam claps again.

Flip! Flop! Clap!

Glad, the crab, and the clam play all day.

Then Glad sees a tiny baby dolphin. Did you know baby dolphins are born tail-first? Tail comes first, then the nose!

"Hello, baby," says Glad. "Can you flip?"

The baby flips. Splash!

The crab claps his claws. The clam claps too.

Glad is glad. Flip! Flop! Clap! Click!

The blue sea is the best place to play.

transcript.title: Night at the Dinosaur Hall
transcript.text:
Maya won a contest: one whole night sleeping in the dinosaur hall!

She spread her sleeping bag beneath the great long-necked skeleton. The lights went low. The room grew quiet.

Then she heard a creak.

The huge beast lowered its head and peered down at her. "Do you mean to sleep right there?" it said.

Maya squeaked. "You can speak?"

"Only at night," the dinosaur said. "Come. I will teach you what the signs leave out."

They roamed the hall. The dinosaur explained how it reached the highest leaves, how its team moved in a herd, and how it drank from a stream each dawn.

"Scientists keep learning new things about us," it said proudly. "Each year they find more."

At daybreak the bones went still again.

Maya rolled up her sleeping bag, beaming. She had the best dream — or maybe it was real.
transcript.cover_scene: A girl in a sleeping bag looking up at a towering long-necked dinosaur skeleton in a dim museum hall at night.

chapters.title: Plip the Sea Turtle's Big Plan
chapters.text:
Plip is a small sea turtle. Plip has a big plan.

"I will swim to the flat black rock," says Plip. "Plan, plan, my big plan!"

Plip flaps. Plip flips. Plip glides past a blue crab.

"Clip clap!" snaps the crab. "That is a long swim!"

"I am glad to try," says Plip. "Plan, plan, my big plan!"

Plip swims past a clam. Plip swims past a flag of green weed.

Splash! A dolphin plays close by. "Come play!" says the dolphin.

"Not yet," says Plip. "Plan, plan, my big plan!"

Plip climbs up on the flat black rock. Plip flops down in the sun.

The crab claps. The clam claps. The dolphin splashes.

Did you know? Sea turtles can swim for miles and miles! That is a true fact.

"I did it," grins Plip. "Plan, plan, my BIG plan!"

transcript.title: Louder Than Thunder
transcript.text:
"Rockets are louder than thunder," Maya announced at breakfast.

"How loud is that?" Dad asked.

"Loud enough to shake the ground," she said. "Loud enough to wake a dinosaur."

So Maya built one. She taped three paper towel tubes together, painted them gleaming white, and drew a green dinosaur on the side.

She named it the Dino Streak.

Out on the driveway, she counted down. "Three… two… one… blast off!"

She threw the rocket high. It sailed above the mailbox, above the oak tree, and landed in a heap of leaves.

Maya cheered so loudly that a crow flew off the roof.

That night she dreamed her rocket reached the moon. A long-necked dinosaur waited there, munching moon leaves, and waved a tiny claw as she flew past.

"See you again soon!" Maya called, and her voice boomed louder than thunder.
transcript.cover_scene: A girl in a driveway launching a homemade paper rocket painted with a green dinosaur, autumn leaves swirling around her.

chapters.title: Jane and the Bubble Rocket
chapters.text:
Jane made a rocket from a tube. She gave it a nose and a fin.

"Take my rocket to the lake," said Jane. "It can ride on bubbles!"

NASA kids make bubble rockets too. Pop! The bubbles shake, and up the rocket goes.

Jane shook the tube. She set it on a stone. She made a wish.

Five. Four. Three. Two. One!

The rocket rose like a kite. It flew past the pine tree. It flew past the gate.

"Wave to it!" said Jane. Her pal Mike gave a big wave.

The rocket came down in the lake. Splash! A fine wave rose up.

A dolphin came to take a look. She gave the rocket a nudge with her nose.

"That dolphin likes my rocket!" said Jane.

Jane and Mike made five more. Each one rose up, up, up.

"Same time next time?" said Mike.

"Yes!" said Jane. "We will make a huge one!"
